sec: Complications and clinical pearls of hypothyroidism

items.q: Match the following complication to its source description — 1) Myxoedema coma 2) Hashimoto encephalopathy 3) Carpal tunnel syndrome 4) Hypocholesterolaemia (printed label, unusual) … A) Decompensated severe hypothyroidism B) Steroid-responsive neuropsychiatric syndrome C) Most common cause in females D) Cardiovascular risk-related feature (page label)
items.exp: Myxoedema coma is decompensated severe hypothyroidism; Hashimoto encephalopathy is a steroid-responsive neuropsychiatric syndrome; CTS is the most common cause in females per the page; hypocholesterolaemia is the page's own label (note: hypothyroid patients typically have hypercholesterolaemia, an inconsistency the source labels as 'hypocholesterolaemia'). (Book p907)

items.q: An 80-year-old woman is found hypothermic, bradycardic and obtunded in winter; TSH is markedly elevated. The most consistent diagnosis is:
items.exp: Decompensated severe hypothyroidism with hypothermia and obtundation fits myxoedema coma. (Book p907)

items.q: Assess myxoedema coma: I It carries a high mortality even with treatment. II IV levothyroxine plus glucocorticoids is a typical emergency regimen.
items.exp: Myxoedema coma has high mortality; empiric IV levothyroxine (often combined with liothyronine) plus stress-dose hydrocortisone is the source's emergency regimen. (Book p907)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among complications where hypothyroidism affects the central nervous system?
items.exp: Hypocholesterolaemia is a metabolic label, not a CNS complication; the others are neurological. (Book p907)

items.q: Per the page's most-common-cause note, carpal tunnel syndrome in females is most often caused by ___.
items.exp: The page states hypothyroidism is the most common cause of CTS in females, with amyloidosis as the most common cause in males. (Book p907)

items.q: Match the following effusions/comorbidities to the source's hypothyroid complications list — 1) Pleural 2) Pericardial 3) Ascites 4) Oligomenorrhoea … A) Serous cavity collection B) Reproductive disturbance C) Refractory to diuretics per source D) Same column
items.exp: Pleural and pericardial effusions are common serous cavity collections; ascites is sometimes refractory to diuretics per the page; oligomenorrhoea / amenorrhoea is a reproductive disturbance. (Book p907)

items.q: A hypothyroid patient has recurrent large-volume pleural and pericardial effusions that do not improve with diuretics. Which mechanism is most consistent with the source?
opts: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
items.exp: Hypothyroid effusions are typically myxoedematous, with high protein content and poor response to diuretics. (Book p907)

items.q: Assess cardiac effects: I Hypothyroidism causes bradycardia. II Pericardial effusion is a recognised complication.
items.exp: Bradycardia and pericardial effusion are both listed; long-standing hypothyroidism can cause pericardial effusion with cardiac tamponade rarely. (Book p907)

items.q: Match the following complication to the most likely clinical context — 1) Obstructive sleep apnoea 2) Carpal tunnel syndrome 3) Myxoedema coma 4) Hashimoto encephalopathy … A) Common in obese hypothyroid adults B) Most common cause of CTS in females C) Decompensated hypothyroid with hypothermia D) Steroid-responsive neuropsychiatric syndrome
items.exp: OSA is common in obese hypothyroid adults; CTS in females is mostly due to hypothyroidism; myxoedema coma presents with hypothermia; Hashimoto encephalopathy is the steroid-responsive neuropsychiatric syndrome. (Book p907)

items.q: A 70-year-old hypothyroid on levothyroxine has increasing pericardial effusion. The most appropriate next step is:
opts: Assess cardiac tamponade and ensure euthyroidism
Increase methimazole to lower TSH further
items.exp: Effusions can progress even on treatment; assess haemodynamics (tamponade) and ensure adequate replacement rather than stopping therapy. (Book p907)

items.q: Atypical pericardial effusion that is high-protein and slow-accumulating in hypothyroid patients is called ___.
items.exp: Myxoedema pericardial effusion is the eponymous hypothyroid entity; it can be large but tamponade is uncommon. (Book p907)

items.q: Assess the source's gender note: I Hypothyroidism is the most common cause of CTS in females. II Amyloidosis is the most common cause of CTS in males per the source.
items.exp: Both statements reflect the page's gender-stratified most-common-cause list for carpal tunnel syndrome. (Book p907)
